props.gloss_en: the mishnah: salted food brought first with bread -- he blesses over the salted food and exempts the bread, for the bread is secondary to it
Rav Ashi: they taught it of those who eat fruits of Genosar

Rabba bar bar Chana: when we went after R' Yochanan to eat Genosar fruit, a hundred of us brought him ten each and ten of us a hundred each; every hundred filled a three-se'a basket, and he ate them all
(entertained, as the words stand) R' Yochanan swore he had not tasted ziyuna
rather say: R' Yochanan swore he had not tasted mezona
R' Abbahu ate [Genosar fruit] until a fly would slide off his forehead
R' Ami and R' Asi would eat until their hair fell out
R' Shimon ben Lakish would eat until he was dazed; R' Yochanan would tell the Nasi's household, and R' Yehuda Nesia would send officers after him and bring him home
Rav Dimi: King Yannai had a city on the King's Mountain from which they took 600,000 bowls of small fish for the fig-cutters from Shabbat eve to Shabbat eve
Ravin: King Yannai had a tree on the King's Mountain from which they took down forty se'a of pigeons from three broods each month
R' Yitzchak: there was a city in the Land of Israel named Gufnit with eighty pairs of priest-brothers married to eighty pairs of priest-sisters

the Rabbis searched from Sura to Nehardea and found none but Rav Chisda's daughters, married to Rami bar Chama and Mar Ukva bar Chama -- and though the sisters were priestesses, the husbands were not priests
Rav: any meal in which there is no salt is not a meal
R' Yochanan: any meal in which there is no sharif is not a meal

objections.gloss_en: ומי איכא מידי דהוי מליח עיקר ופת טפלה? -- is there anything where salted food is primary and bread secondary?
